searchText: Summary of goerli-shadow-fork-6: - No client issues, all combinations are synced and at head + processed the transition correctly - Two nodes ran out of disk space (🤦) and that explains the drop in participation rate - ~30% of the network ran mev_boost through the transition, we noticed no issues other than higher latency on one node in India - potentially a defective machine. Great work everyone! 🙌 Should execution clients stop propagating TTD blocks after first finality or second finality? After the first one. And after the second one, peers that are keep sending NewBlock and NewBlockHashes messages should be penalised > Beginning with receiving the finalized block next to the FIRST_FINALIZED_BLOCK, I read this as the second finalized block, is this written clearly or not? What is a finalized block? First block after the first finalized epoch? Or maybe second block within the finalized epoch? Ok, so finalized block may not be final? terminology here becomes very fuzzy 🙂 I'm tcpdumping the localhost engine API between teku and geth on a post-bellatrix pair, and see periodic calls for `eth_getBlockByNumber`, I'm guessing that is used for TTD tracking? Also seeing `engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1` and not seeing any warnings in either log, so safe to assume this pair looks good for the goerli merge? We'll call eth_getBlockByNumber both for TTD tracking and for tracking deposits. And yes if you're not seeing warnings then it's ready for the merge.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
Summary of goerli-shadow-fork-6:
- No client issues, all combinations are synced and at head + processed the transition correctly
- Two nodes ran out of disk space (🤦) and that explains the drop in participation rate
- ~30% of the network ran mev_boost through the transition, we noticed no issues other than higher latency on one node in India - potentially a defective machine.
